item.title: Interpret a noisy office sample
item.summary: Two colleagues discuss selection bias in feedback on a new workplace layout.
item.transcript_text:
Mina: The new layout got high scores for quietness. Is that enough to recommend it to the other teams?
Omar: The people we asked had booked focus rooms. Colleagues on the open desks, where noise matters most, were missing.
Mina: We could include open-desk users next time and walk around to take sound readings.
Omar: Yes, and collect reports at comparable times. A quiet Friday afternoon doesn't tell us how Tuesday's customer calls will sound.
Mina: In other words, we can keep the focus rooms as a promising part of the pilot, but the larger recommendation stays provisional.
Omar: That's the distinction we should put in the board note.

options: Most respondents used the open desks
There were no scores for quietness
The survey mainly reached people using focus rooms
The feedback came from customer calls
questions.explanation: Omar says the surveyed people had booked focus rooms and did not include open-desk colleagues.

options: Noise patterns can vary during the working week
Focus rooms never open on Friday
Sound readings can only be taken on Tuesdays
Customer calls always stop in the afternoon
questions.explanation: Omar contrasts a quiet Friday afternoon with periods of customer calls.

questions.prompt: What goes in the board note?
options: The whole layout has been proven effective
The focus rooms are promising while the wider case remains open
The survey must be thrown away in full
Noise measurements now establish a company-wide standard
questions.explanation: The final exchange separates a narrow promising finding from the provisional wider recommendation.
